[highlight]Phase-Bridge 15 Landing Pads
[gold]3.0
[white]

Also known as the Core-Adjacent 15-Pad Receiver.

[lightgray]
unable to stack.
Total throughput: 300.
Phase bridges provide perfectly balanced distribution.

Four phase bridges handle transport, while stacked dual phase bridges return items to the core.

By adjusting the stacked dual phase bridges, the design can be placed directly adjacent to the core.

* Sequential Landing Control

Requires at least one Flare to detect the core.

When landing pads become bottlenecked due to insufficient launch throughput, the sequential-switching logic dynamically adjusts the received item type according to core inventory, prioritizing the least-stocked resources first.
In Campaign, this allows launch throughput to remain fully utilized.

Link the logic to a message block to monitor switching status.

Sand, scrap, coal, and spores are excluded from launch selection by default.

blueprints.name: Linux on mlogv32
blueprints.author: Iliary
blueprints.description:
This schematic contains a fully functional 32-bit RISC-V emulator that runs Linux.

In this configuration, it has 16 MiB of ROM, 14 MiB of RAM, a 70x38 character text-only display, a keyboard (sortKB), and four 16550A UART ports (though only one is currently accessible from Linux).

To use, simply build the schematic, wait a few seconds to let all of the processors initialize, then turn on the switch labeled POWER_SWITCH. Log in with the username root. Set your FPS limit to 60 for best results.

On my machine, it takes about 8 minutes from power on to the login prompt, and the game runs at ~10 FPS when the CPU is not idle. The filesystem is read-only (stored in ROM via cramfs), so /tmp is the only place where you can create files. Also, the display doesn't support escape codes, so backspace and color codes will look weird.

Requires b149.
